players.note: Antonio Williams enthusiasts have been eagerly awaiting a production spike for the rookie, and maybe we'll get a big game from him Monday night against the Bengals. In the three games since Commanders WR Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon, ending his season, Williams has had 10-121-1 on 15 targets, with a 14.4% target share. The good news is that Williams' snap shares over his last three games have been 83%, 84% and 86%. He's a full-time receiver now, attached to a good quarterback in Jayden Daniels. Williams also has a juicy stretch of schedule coming up. In Week 12, the rookie faces the Cardinals. Arizona's pass defense ranks 31st in defense-adjusted value over average (DVOA). In Week 13, Williams faces a Titans defense that has allowed more fantasy points per game to wide receivers than any other team in the league. And in Week 14, Williams faces the Texans, who have allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to receivers.

In the two games that Dolphins QB Malik Willis has spent on injured reserve, rookie WR Caleb Douglas has had 3-71-0 on eight targets vs. the Colts and 2-30-0 on 10 targets while playing with inexperienced backup Kyle McCord. A third-round rookie, Douglas has looked like a future star at times this season. Week 11 was not one of those times, as the normally sure-handed Douglas dropped a couple of passes and seemed out of sync with McCord. Still, it was encouraging that Douglas had a 30.3% target share on Sunday. Douglas has a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. When he faced the Jets in Week 7, Douglas had 2-70-2 on three targets, with one of his two touchdowns a 63-yarder. With the favorable matchup this week, Douglas is a potential starter. He probably won't be playable in a Week 13 matchup against the Broncos, but Douglas could be back in play against the Bears in Week 14, and the Dolphins could get Willis back for that contest.

Last week's bye-pocalypse forced a lot of fantasy managers to make some tough cuts. The Yahoo rostership of promising rookie Omar Cooper Jr. slipped below 50%. Cooper missed Week 11 with an ankle injury and may or may not return for the Jets' Week 12 matchup against the Dolphins. If Cooper isn't back this week, there's a good chance he'll return after the Jets' Week 13 bye, but he would be walking back into a tough Week 14 matchup against the Broncos. That's why it's not worth spending a great deal of FAAB on Cooper. But the appeal is that Cooper flashed some serious potential with back-to-back 100-yard receiving games with a touchdown in Weeks 6 and 7. It's possible Cooper offers more upside than some of the other wide receivers on your roster.

Kaelon Black's run of three consecutive games with double-digit carries came to an end in Week 11, when he had 6-8-0 rushing and 1-7-0 on one target against the Vikings. You'd think Black would have gotten more work in a 35-10 victory, but he played only 16 of San Francisco's 48 offensive snaps. If Black has stand-alone fantasy value, it's the sort of low-level value that might only come in handy in weeks when there are teams on bye. This is not such a week, so if you pick up Black, it's probably not with the intention of starting him right away. But Black is the single most essential handcuff running back in fantasy. If Christian McCaffrey were to miss time, Black would be enormously valuable as the lead back in Kyle Shanahan's well-oiled offense. Black's enormous potential upside makes him well worth a roster spot if he remains unrostered in your league.

Justice Hill has had a handful of good games for the Ravens this season. He had a 73-yard rushing day against the Falcons in Week 5, 85 rushing yards and a touchdown against the Jaguars in Week 9, and 96 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown against the Panthers in Week 11. But Hill hasn't logged double-digit carries in a game this season, and he's had 38 or fewer scrimmage yards in eight of his 11 games. With his spotty production profile, Hill isn't worth rostering.

Third-round rookie Ted Hurst played his best game of the season for the Buccaneers on Sunday, finishing with 5-56-2 on seven targets. Hurst reliably got himself open and made some terrific plays on the ball. Hurst was third in snaps and routes among the Tampa Bay receivers in Week 11, but not that far behind Emeka Egbuka. Chris Godwin led the Buccaneers' receivers in both categories. A big-play receiver with a 6-foot-3 frame and 4.42 speed, Hurst could surge down the stretch. It's also possible he could be thwarted by the limitations of QB Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers' passing game. Hurst is an intriguing speculative addition.

With WR Puka Nacua on injured reserve and WR Davante Adams not expected back from his hamstring injury, someone has to catch passes for the Rams in their Wednesday-night game against the Packers. Rams head coach Sean McVay has leaned heavily into multiple-TE use, and with Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve, veteran Tyler Higbee is the Rams' top pass-catching tight end. With Nacua and Adams out in Week 10, Higbee led the Rams' tight ends with four targets and had three catches for 17 yards and a touchdown. For the season, Higbee has 31-304-2 on 43 targets. The Packers have been stingy against TEs this season, allowing 8.0 half-point PPR fantasy points per game to the position. But the paucity of pass-catching options for Rams QB Matthew Stafford should keep Higbee involved this week and in the weeks to come.

Dylan Sampson is by no means a potential league winner, but he has some low-level stand-alone value in PPR leagues, and Sampson would become an every-week fantasy starter if anything were to happen to the Browns' starting running back, Quinshon Judkins. In the four games since Sampson returned from a knee injury, he's had 19-79-0 rushing, with no more than eight carries in any of those games. But he's been productive as a pass-catcher, with 16-152-0 on 22 targets. Sampson has had at least three receptions and 27 receiving yards in all four of those games.

Pat Freiermuth gets a favorable Week 12 matchup against a TE-funnel Denver defense that entered Week 11 having allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy points per game to wide receivers but the fourth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends. Freiermuth had 5-39-0 on five targets Sunday vs. the Eagles. He hasn't had more than 46 receiving yards in a game all season, but Freiermuth has scored six touchdowns. He sometimes gets tush-push carries for the Steelers at the goal line. Although Freiermuth shares TE targets with Darnell Washington, Freiermuth usually runs more routes and draws more targets than Washington.

Darren Waller is an unpredictable and TD-centric performer who's had games of 19.0, 16.8 and 11.5 half-point PPR fantasy points this season but has also produced 5.1 or fewer fantasy points in five games. The net result is that Waller is tied with Tucker Kraft for TE14 in half-point PPR fantasy points per game. Waller gets a Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers, who entered Week 11 having allowed the eighth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends despite having a top defense. When Waller faced the Buccaneers in Week 7, he had only one catch, but it went for a 50-yard touchdown. You could conceivably stream Waller this week against the Bucs, but he won't be in play in Week 13 against a Vikings defense that stifles tight ends.

We continue to believe that if there's a Houston Texans receiver worth rostering other than Nico Collins, it's Xavier Hutchinson. Over his last three games, Hutchinson's snap shares have been 81.4%, 76.1% and 81.8%. That's significant, since Texans offensive coordinator Nick Calley uses a WR rotation that tends to thwart the fantasy value of all the Houston receivers. Hutchinson had a disappointing 2-13-0 on three targets in the Texans' Week 11 win over the Colts, but CJ Stroud threw only 27 passes in a blowout victory. Hutchinson had scored a touchdown in each of his three previous games. The Texans have a home matchup against the stumbling Ravens this week.

Bhayshul Tuten has been playing with an ankle injury that he appeared to aggravate Sunday in the Jaguars' loss to the Giants. If Tuten is unable to answer the bell for Week 4, Chris Rodriguez Jr. would be in line for a heavy workload against the Titans. With Tuten staking his claim to Jacksonville's lead-back role, Rodriguez hasn't gotten more than 11 rushing attempts in a game all season. He has 63-261-4 rushing and 4-49-0 receiving for the year. Rodriguez is capable of taking on a bigger workload. Last season, Rodriguez had double-digit carries in six of the Jaguars' last seven regular-season games and punched in five touchdowns over that stretch. The Jaguars will be heavy home favorites against the Titans this week, potentially setting up a run-friendly game script. If Tuten is able to play, the Jaguars might lighten his load by giving Rodriguez a heavier allotment of carries. Even with no teams on bye, Rodriguez can be a usable fantasy option in Week 12.

Saquon Barkley left the Eagles' Week 11 win over the Steelers with a shoulder injury believed to be a stinger. Barkley indicated after the game that he expected to play in Week 12, but the Eagles have a quick turnaround with a Thanksgiving Day game against the Cowboys in Dallas. It's possible the 3-7 Eagles will opt to play it safe with their star running back. Will Shipley was back in action in Week 11 after missing four games with a partial tear of his plantar fascia in his foot. Shipley was a hot waiver target in Week 5 after Barkley sustained a hamstring injury in Week 4, but Shipley wound up leaving the Eagles' Week 5 loss to the Jaguars early with the foot injury. Dameon Pierce led Philadelphia in carries that day. Pierce is no longer on the roster, and Jaydon Blue is currently the Eagles' No. 3 running back. Shipley has only 64 carries over three NFL seasons. He's an athletic former Clemson standout capable of contributing as a pass-catcher. Monitor the status of Barkley and scale your bids on Shipley accordingly.

The Cardinals' offense has become such a sinkhole that it's hard to recommend anyone other than TE Trey McBride for fantasy usage. But those of you in deeper leagues might find some utility in Bam Knight. Knight has been splitting work with Tyler Allgeier in the absence of first-round rookie Jeremiyah Love, who's out with an ankle injury. Love is eligible to return from injured reserve in Week 13, but the 3-8 Cardinals have little incentive to bring back the No. 3 overall pick and further risk his health near the end of an injury-marred season. A former undrafted free agent out of North Carolina State, the 25-year-old Knight has 40-222-0 rushing this season and is averaging 5.6 yards per carry. Allgeier is averaging 4.0 yards per carry, but if you exclude his 147-yard rushing performance against the Cowboys in Week 8, Allgeier is averaging just 2.9 yards per carry. Knight has become the Cardinals' primary early-down back, while Allgeier plays primarily on passing downs. The impotence of the Arizona offense keeps Knight from being an appealing Week 12 option. But it's worth noting that after the Cardinals' Week 14 bye, their next three games are against the Jets, Saints and Raiders, all of whom have atrocious run defenses. If the Cardinals wisely shelve Love for the rest of the season, Knight might be a sneaky RB option in the fantasy playoffs.

Marginalized in the Titans' offense by the offseason arrival of slot receiver Wan'Dale Robinson. Chimere Dike is playing a prominent role for Tennessee now that Robinson is out for the season with an ankle injury. After a surprisingly productive 2025 rookie season in which he had 48-423-4 on 74 targets, Dike played 13 or fewer offensive snaps in each of the Titans' first seven games this season. But with Robinson out, Dike has played more than 50 offensive snaps in each of his last three games, producing 13-156-1 on 16 targets over that span. Dike has also had two rushing attempts for nine yards over his last two games. Dike was lined up outside on 79.4% of his offensive snaps in Weeks 9-10, per Fantasy Points Data. With rookie WR Carnell Tate sidelined by a shoulder injury in those two games, Dike filled in as the Z receiver. But with Tate back in Week 11, Dike moved back into the slot in 11 personnel — a more natural role for his talents — and had 6-69-0 on seven targets vs. the Cowboys. Dike also played eight snaps in 12 personnel, according to PFF's Nate Jahnke. With his expanded role, Dike might be able to provide help in deeper leagues down the stretch.

Running back handcuffing can be a suboptimal strategy because it means dedicating two valuable roster spots to a single position on a single team. But the later in the season it gets, the more handcuffing a starting running back makes sense — as long as that running back has a clear backup. The clear backup to Chase Brown in Cincinnati is Samaje Perine, and if Brown were to go down, Perine would be the lead back in one of the NFL's most potent offenses.

Devaughn Vele played more snaps than heralded rookie Jordyn Tyson in Week 11, ran more than twice as many routes, and finished with 7-76-0 on seven targets in the Saints' 21-13 loss to the Bears. Tyson played 45 snaps in Week 10 and had 11-80-0 on 13 targets vs. the Panthers, so it's hard to get a handle on the Saints' WR usage. Tyson may have played limited snaps on Sunday because of a chest injury that had him officially limited in a couple of practices last week. There's a good chance Vele is the Saints' No. 3 the rest of the way. It's not worth chasing his Week 11 numbers.

It's not that we shouldn't believe in Jack Bech. It's that we shouldn't believe in Bech after just one good game. Bech had a breakthrough 8-88-1 performance against the Broncos on Sunday. With Brock Bowers out, the Raiders played a lot of 11 personnel with three receivers. Bech, Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor ended up with similar snap, route and target counts. Obviously, the absence of Bowers funneled some extra targets to the Las Vegas WRs. It's good to see positive results for the second-year receiver whose rookie season was a washout. But it's too early to chase Bech on waivers.

Bills passing-down back Ty Johnson had 1-2-0 rushing and 7-55-0 receiving vs. the Dolphins on Sunday. Don't chase the receiving stats. Johnson hasn't had more than four catches in any other game this season.

With Puka Nacua expected to miss the rest of the regular season after having knee surgery, and with Davante Adams not expected back from his hamstring injury until Week 13 at the earliest, Konata Mumpfield could have short-term value as Rams QB Matthew Stafford's de facto No. 1 receiver. In the Rams' most recent game before their Week 11 bye, Mumpfield led the Rams' receivers with a 64% snap share and had 3-81-0 on four targets. When Nacua was injured and missed a couple of games early in the season, Mumpfield had 4-93-1 on eight targets against the Broncos in Week 3. It's hard to predict what Stafford's target distribution will look like this week against the Packers, but Mumpfield is an intriguing young receiver who could have a substantial role in Week 12 and perhaps beyond.

The Rams have activated Terrance Ferguson from injured reserve so that his 21-day window to return from injured reserve wouldn't close, forcing him to miss the rest of the season. But Rams head coach Sean McVay has indicated that Ferguson is not expected to play in Week 12, and it's possible Ferguson's hamstring injury keeps him out longer. Still, with Puka Nacua out for the season, the athletic Ferguson could become a prominent contributor to the Rams' passing game upon his return. When Nacua was out in Week 2, Ferguson had 6-54-1 on nine targets against the Giants. Ferguson injured his ankle the next week against the Broncos, was on the verge of returning a few weeks ago, then hurt his hamstring in practice.

Undrafted free agent rookie Max Hurleman had 6-61-1 on seven targets for the Steelers on Sunday in his NFL debut. Hurleman was fourth in snaps and routes among the Pittsburgh wide receivers. Despite his seemingly instant rapport with Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers, Hurleman is not a good bet for continued fantasy production.
